AGENDA
  JOINT MEETING: GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL AND GLENDALE HOUSING AUTHORITY
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
 verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
 glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
 using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
 archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office.
 If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the
 City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  NOVEMBER 2, 2021 AT 2:00 PM

To help slow the transmission of COVID-19, and protect the health and safety of the community, City
Council, as well as Board & Commission meetings, will continue to be closed to the public for in-person
attendance.
The public is encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social
distancing. Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and
AT&T U-verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu.
For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100 or (833) 979-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed.

  - 2:00 PM
  - Report of the City Clerk of the City Council and Housing Authority, re: Posting of Agenda.
  The Agenda for the Tuesday, November 2, 2021 joint public meeting of the City Council and
  Housing Authority was posted on October 26, 2021 on the Bulletin Board outside City Hall

  A JOINT PUBLIC MEETING of the City Council and Housing Authority is hereby
  called to meet at 2:00 PM on Tuesday, November 2, 2021, in the Council Chamber, 613 E.
  Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206 to Consider the Following Item(s) of Business, to
  wit;

  1. Community Development, re: Proposal to Adopt a Relocation Plan for Housing
  Authority Owned Land at 912 E. Broadway in Glendale, California 91205 in Support of
  Harrower Village, a 40-Unit, 100% Affordable, Rental Housing Project Reserved for
  Seniors
  a. Housing Authority Resolution to Approve a Relocation Plan for Housing Authority Owned
  Land at 912 E. Broadway in Glendale, California 91205
  b. Council Motion to Approve an Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with
  Overland, Pacific and Cutler, LLC (Contract No. 8001108) in the Amount of $66,778 for a
  New Not-to-Exceed Amount of $246,778
  c. Council Resolution of Appropriation in the Amount of $50,000 to increase the City’s
  contract with Overland, Pacific & Cutler, LLC
  2. Community Development, re: Membership in California Public Finance Authority
  Joint Powers Authority and Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act Public Hearing
  for California Public Finance Authority Proposed Issuance of Approximately $33
  Million in Tax Exempt Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds in Support of Citrus
  Crossing (900 E. Broadway), a Glendale Senior Affordable Housing Project to be
  Constructed, Operated and Maintained by 900 E Broadway, L.P., a Partnership
  Created by Meta Housing Corporation
  a. City Council Resolution to Approve, Authorize and Direct Execution of a Joint Exercise of
  Powers Agreement Relating to the California Public Finance Authority, Making Glendale an
  Additional Member
  b. City Council Resolution to Approve the Issuance by the California Public Finance
  Authority of Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds in Aggregate Principal Amount Not to
  Exceed $33 Million for the Purpose of Financing the Construction or Improvement of Citrus
  Crossing
  3. Community Services and Parks, re: Status of Program Planning for the FY 2022-23,
  CDBG, ESG and HOME Annual Action Plan and shift in funds from the cancelled FY
  2018-2019 CDBG Project to the FY 2021-22 CDBG Project
  a. City Council Motion approving the FY 2022-23 CDBG program priorities; a FY 2022-23
  Proposed CDBG Funding Allocation Plan by Funding Category; and issuance of an RFP to
  community agencies for CDBG Public Social Services and CDBG Capital Improvement
  Projects

  11 02 21
  2  CC HA
   b. Housing Authority Motion approving the FY 2022-23 CDBG program priorities; a FY
  2022-23 Proposed CDBG Funding Allocation Plan by Funding Category; and issuance of
  an RFP to community agencies for CDBG Public Social Services and CDBG Capital
  Improvement Projects
  c. City Council Motion to amend the current FY 2021-22 CDBG Annual Action Plan to
  reprogram $65,000 from canceled FY 2018-19 Adventist Health Glendale Windows Project
  to the currently funded FY2021-22 YMCA of Glendale First Floor All-Inclusive Locker Room
  Project, as recommended by the CDBG Advisory Committee
  d. City Council Resolution of Appropriation in the amount of $65,000 to shift the returned
  CDBG funds from the canceled FY 2018-2019 Adventist Health Glendale Windows Project
  to the FY 2021-22 YMCA of Glendale First Floor All-Inclusive Locker Room Project, as
  recommended by the CDBG Advisory Committee
  4. Community Services and Parks, re: HUD Section 108 Loan Guarantee Program
  Application for Fremont Park Renovation Project
  a. City Council Resolution authorizing the City Manager or a designee to submit a Section
  108 Loan Guarantee application to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban
  Development (HUD) in the amount of $4,000,000 with a ten-year repayment term to be
  used for the proposed Fremont Park Renovation Project; and to execute such documents
  as may be required in order to implement the application
  5. Community Services and Parks, re: Approval of Funding Recommendations by the
  Glendale Continuum of Care (CoC) Board for the Submission of the Glendale CoC
  Funding Application to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, as
  part of the 2021 CoC Notice of Funding Opportunity competition
  a. Council Motion to approve the 2021 Continuum of Care (CoC) Program Priorities, and
  authorize the submission of a grant application to the Federal Department of Housing and
  Urban Development (HUD), on behalf of the Glendale CoC, under the 2021 CoC program
  competition, as recommended by the CoC Board; and authorize the City Manager or a
  designee to execute all agreements, certifications, and documents necessary to accept and
  implement the funding
  b. Housing Authority Motion to approve the 2021 Continuum of Care (CoC) Program
  Priorities, and authorize the submission of a grant application to the Federal Department of
  Housing and Urban Development (HUD), on behalf of the Glendale CoC, under the 2021
  CoC program competition, as recommended by the CoC Board; and authorize the City
  Manager or a designee to execute all agreements, certifications, and documents necessary
  to accept and implement the funding
